LESSON: READING 7.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.2: Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information, part of Strand 7 in Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we read to find information from texts efficiently? 2. Why should we engage in sports and games?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. answer questions from texts for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. create a personal collection of vocabulary related to the theme for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. summarise the key ideas from texts for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. embrace the acquisition of knowledge on sports and games through reading.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. answer questions from texts for information,

B. create a personal collection of vocabulary related to the theme for comprehension,

   Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. summarise the key ideas from texts for information,

   Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. embrace the acquisition of knowledge on sports and games through reading.

   Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search from online and offline sources for short passages on sports and games,

2. conduct a silent reading session to read short passages related to the theme,

3. answer direct and inferential questions on the short passages read,

4. work collaboratively to prepare flashcards with the vocabulary identified from the passage,

5. display the flashcards for peers to read aloud,

6. make notes on the main ideas from texts. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search from online and offline sources for short passages on sports and games,
2. conduct a silent reading session to read short passages related to the theme,
3. answer direct and inferential questions on the short passages read,
4. work collaboratively to prepare flashcards with the vocabulary identified from the passage,
5. display the flashcards for peers to read aloud,
6. make notes on the main ideas from texts. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 7.2.1 Reading for information together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: The learner plans and manages tasks effectively while displaying the flashcards for peers to read aloud.

• Digital Literacy: This is achieved as the learner interacts with digital content to search for short passages on sports and

games.

Values:
• Love: This is promoted as the learner works collaboratively to prepare flashcards with the vocabulary identified from the

passage.

• Responsibility: This is achieved as the learner diligently searches from online and offline sources for short passages on sports

and games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Human Rights: This is promoted as the learner is exposed to texts on sports and games which is a key aspect of good health as a

human right.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the vocabulary acquired from texts related to Sports and Games to their learning in Creative Arts and

Sports.
